evals.prompt: The design for the rate limiter is approved and lives at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-20-rate-limiter-design.md (in the input files). Write the implementation plan for it and save it under docs/superpowers/plans/.
evals.expected_output: A plan file at docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-20-rate-limiter.md (or similar name) with the required header including a Spec path and a Global Constraints section quoting the spec's exact values (120/min, burst 20, env var names, Python 3.11+, FastAPI 0.110+); one task per architecture unit, each with Files, Interfaces, and TDD steps whose test steps carry real test code with the spec's values and whose implementation steps name the exact signature and file, with a body only where the signature and tests do not determine the algorithm; no placeholders; consistent function and class names across tasks; ends by offering execution options.
expectations: Plan starts with the header block containing Goal, Architecture, Tech Stack, Spec (a path), and a Global Constraints section

Global Constraints copies exact values from the spec verbatim: 120 requests per minute, burst 20, RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE, RATE_LIMIT_BURST, Python 3.11+, FastAPI 0.110+, no new runtime dependencies, no sleeping in tests
Every task has a Files block with exact paths and an Interfaces block with Consumes/Produces naming exact signatures

Implementation steps name the exact signature (name, parameters, return type) and file, and carry a code body only for an algorithm the signature and tests do not determine (the token-bucket refill arithmetic qualifies; a constructor or a header-setting line does not); no step says 'add tests', 'handle errors', 'similar to Task N', TODO, or TBD

Test steps carry complete test code, compilable as written, with the spec's exact values and the fixtures, helpers and imports they need; a commented outline or a fixture described only in prose is a failure
Class and function names (TokenBucket, try_consume, BucketRegistry) are spelled identically in every task that references them
Each task includes explicit run-test steps with the command and the expected outcome (FAIL then PASS) and a commit step
The 429 JSON body and the three X-RateLimit headers from the spec each appear in a test in some task

Response ends by offering the execution options (subagent-driven and inline; a Herdr new-session option only when HERDR_ENV=1) with a request to review the plan and a one-sentence recommendation drawn from the plan, rather than starting implementation

Header has a Review Focus section (at most five lines naming an input or failure mode the spec implies and the expected behavior), and each line is pinned by a test in the task that owns the code; an empty section says none were found
Implementation-code lines (code blocks inside implementation steps) are a small minority of the plan, and no implementation step reproduces a body that the signature and the test already determine
No build, test, or run command is executed while planning, in the repo or in a scratch copy; the plan is checked by reading the spec and the codebase
